scenes.name: Siouxsie and the Banshees
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Fans de Roxy Music que no creían en el igualitarismo punk («No todo el mundo puede hacerlo»): minimalismo por descarte (sin solos, sin finales de batería), guitarra con flanger entre la Velvet y la ducha de Psicosis, la voz gélida de Siouxsie y letras antisentimentales sobre la locura y los suburbios («Suburban Relapse», «Jigsaw Feeling»). The Scream (1978), Join Hands («Icon», el padrenuestro), Kaleidoscope con John McGeoch y Budgie, Juju (1981), su obra cumbre y matriz del gótico (magia, vudú, Halloween), y A Kiss in the Dreamhouse (1982), decadencia fin de siglo y psicodelia inglesa. Siouxsie quería ser «un palo en la rueda de la mediocridad».

podcast.title: Goth Archetype
podcast.body: Siouxsie Sioux's distinctive appearance, featuring black hair and makeup, established her as an archetype for thousands of Goth followers. "With her really striking appearance and her black hair and the makeup, Suzy became an archetype for thousands."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Goth Queen and Riot Grrrl Inspiration
podcast.body: Siouxsie Sioux, referred to as "Suzy Su" in the transcript, was recognized as a "goth queen" and served as an initial inspiration for the Riot Grrrl movement. She was one of the female pioneers of punk and post-punk whose work influenced the later movement. "goth queen Suzy Su"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Involvement in Bill Grundy TV Episode
podcast.body: Siouxsie Sioux was the woman on whom Bill Grundy made advances during the infamous televised encounter with the Sex Pistols. "In fact, if you've ever seen or heard the famous Bill Grundy TV episode with the pistols, the woman Grundy hits on is, in fact, Suzy Su."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Punk Pioneer
podcast.body: Siouxsie Sioux of Siouxsie and the Banshees was a pioneer who took advantage of punk rock values, inspiring many to express themselves regardless of background or gender. "Suzy Su, of Suzy in the Banshee's, members of the Slitz, Pauli Styrene of X-Ray Specks, Chrissy Hinder, the Pretenders, Patty Smith, and so many more. They were all pioneers and they all inspired many people, women, but also men, to do what they did."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women Who Rocked The 90's

podcast.title: Queen of Goth
podcast.body: Siouxsie Sioux is widely regarded as the "Queen of Goth," an acknowledgment of her influential role and iconic status within the Gothic rock movement that started in the late 1970s and early 1980s. "And for many, the Queen of Goth remains Susie Sue of Susie in the Banshees."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sex Pistols Connection
podcast.body: Siouxsie Sioux was recognized as one of the Sex Pistols' earliest fans. She was visibly present in the audience during their notorious television appearance where they controversially swore at the host. "Susie Su is another person with connections to the sex pistols. She was one of their first fans."

xref.title: Debut Performance – September 1976
xref.body: The band made its debut performance in September 1976 with Sid Vicious on drums. Susan Ballion, who later reinvented herself as Siouxsie Sioux, was the vocalist. "He was the drummer for Susie in the Banshees when they made their debut in September of 1976."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Affair with Annik Honoré
xref.body: On October 16, 1979, while playing a gig at Plan K in Brussels, Belgium, Ian met Annik Honoré, a woman described as resembling Siouxsie Sioux. This encounter quickly evolved into a full-blown affair, with Ian frequently fabricating excuses to meet Annik, who subsequently moved to London and worked at the Belgian Embassy, and even toured with the band on their European dates in early 1980. "On October 16, 1979, the band played a gig at a place called Plan K in Brussels, Belgium. This is where Ian met a woman named Anik on a ray."

xref.title: Goth Archetype
xref.body: Siouxsie Sioux, with her striking appearance of black hair, heavy mascara and eyeshadow, and soulful eyes, along with the band name "Banshees" (evoking horror), became an archetype for goths worldwide, establishing them as one of the first-generation goth bands. "Susie made for a striking figure, black hair, lots of mascara, and eyeshadow, big soulful eyes, and the name Banshees conjured up just the right amount of horror. She became an archetype for Goth's Worldwide."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Inspiration for Siouxsie and the Banshees
xref.body: The Sex Pistols were ascendant and had a dedicated group of fans called the Bromley Contingent, which included Susan Ballion (later Siouxsie Sioux). Siouxsie was inspired by the Pistols to form her own punk band and later Siouxsie and the Banshees. "When the Sex Pistols were on the Ascendant, they had a group of fans that followed them everywhere. They were called the Bromley contingent."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Queen of Goth
xref.body: For many fans and critics, Siouxsie Sioux, the lead singer of Siouxsie and the Banshees, holds the title of the "Queen of Goth." This acknowledges her iconic status and significant influence within the Gothic rock scene that emerged in the late 1970s and early 1980s. "And for many, the Queen of Goth remains Susie Sue of Susie in the Banshees."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Sex Pistols' Number One Fan – Bromley Contingent Member
xref.body: Sid was the Sex Pistols' biggest fan and a member of the "Bromley Contingent," a group of dedicated followers that also included future stars like Billy Idol and Siouxsie Sioux. He followed the band everywhere. "Sid became the Sex Pistols number one fan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Siouxsie Sioux as Archetype
xref.body: Singer Siouxsie Sioux's distinctive black hair, makeup, and striking appearance made her an archetype for thousands of Goth followers. "With her really striking appearance and her black hair and the makeup, Suzy became an archetype for thousands."

xref.title: Siouxsie Sioux's Early Band
xref.body: Formed by Susan Ballion (who became Siouxsie Sioux) after being inspired by the Sex Pistols, this punk band featured future Sex Pistols member Sid Vicious on drums. "forming a band called Flowers of Romance, which featured future sex pistols, Sid Vicious on drums."
